prerequisites: Differential and integral calculus in one and several variables

learning_outcomes.text: Provide the theoretical, methodological and practical elements of mechanics from the mathematical-physics perspective, with the objective of modelling analyzing and solving engineering problems. In particular, the kinematics, the statics and the dynamics of point-mass systems will be covered. The basic elements of Lagrangian mechanics will be covered as well.
Develop a thorough understanding of the course topics and the ability to apply the acquired knowledge to real mechanical systems.

Use mathematical tools in engineering problems through the following steps: 1. being able to write the equations of motion for point-mass systems and rigid bodies using both Newtonian and Lagrangian approaches; 2. being able to solve the equations of motion in some important cases; 3. being able to determine the equilibrium configurations of the most important mechanical systems and study their stability; 4. being able to calculate the inertia matrix of a general rigid body and determine its principal axes of inertia.
Successfully undertake subsequent courses in Structural Mechanics, Mechanics of Machines, and Machine Design.
Study the material of later courses, particularly of building science, machine-building and mechanics applied to machines.
Improve the ability to develop independent thought and learning capabilities through individual and collective problem-solving sessions.
Develop communication skills through oral presentations of the topics taught in the course, with the language proper of the basic disciplines of the degree course.

syllabus_topics: Dynamics of the material point, of systems and rigid body

assessment_methods.method: Written practical test (may include theoretical questions)
Written and/or oral theoretical test (may require solution of exercises)

assessment_rules: Assessment will consist of a written practical test and a written and/or oral theoretical test; these may occur simultaneously. The final grade is awarded on a scale of 30, with the possibility of honours. The written test gives a maximum mark of 24 points. Those who pass the written exam with a sufficient score of 18 can choose between two oral methods: a) oral examination limited to the discussion of the written text, allowing a variation of +/- 2 points; b) extended oral exam with 3 questions, allowing an increase of +/- 3 points per question.
